clue.text: It's safer not to stray in this area by the shore

indicators.note: to stray is to wander off, so the letters of safer not wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A warning that it is safer not to wander off along the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to stray' rearranges SAFER NOT; 'It's' and 'in this' simply link the anagram to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A seafront is the promenade or district of a town that faces the sea.

clue.text: What's inside isn't real — only different

indicators.note: different suggests the letters of isn't real are made into something other than they were

explanation.surface: A remark that the interior of something is a sham, only made to look otherwise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges the letters of ISN'T REAL (the apostrophe adds nothing); 'only' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrails are the guts or innards, the organs contained within a body.

clue.text: Sees that the standard is kept up

definitions.text: Sees that the standard is kept up

parts.words: Sees that the standard is kept up
parts.note: reads like a quality inspector maintaining standards, but a standard is a banner, and keeping it raised means displaying it on a pole

explanation.surface: Someone ensures quality does not slip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standard' looks like a level of quality; here it is a flag, hoisted so it stays up. The phrase also means showing patriotic support.
explanation.definitionFit: To display a banner aloft on its pole is literally to keep a standard up.

clue.text: Remnant is substandard, needing price reduction

parts.note: food or work that is off has gone bad or is below par
a cut is a reduction, as in a price cut

explanation.surface: A leftover piece of cloth is poor quality and must be marked down.
explanation.definitionFit: An offcut is a leftover piece trimmed from a larger sheet of material.

clue.text: The expedition set off

explanation.surface: The journey got under way.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip is a journey or outing; to trip an alarm or switch is to activate or trigger it.

clue.text: Runners allowed to enter various heats

indicators.note: to enter means one piece goes into the middle of another
various suggests the letters of heats take a different arrangement

parts.note: to let someone do something is to allow it

explanation.surface: Competitors are permitted to take part in several qualifying races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heats' looks like races, matching 'Runners', but its letters are only fodder: 'various' turns them into ATHES, and 'to enter' places the permission word inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Track athletes compete in races, so runners are a familiar example.

clue.text: Half-built residence?

parts.note: suggests an unfinished house, but means a house built as one half of a joined pair

explanation.walkthrough: A semi-detached house shares a wall with its neighbour, so it is half of a single building; 'semi' also means half.
explanation.definitionFit: A British semi is a semi-detached house, one of two homes joined under a single roof.

clue.text: They don't believe he requires foreign capital

parts.note: the capital of Greece is foreign to a British setter

explanation.surface: A man insists on going abroad to a capital city, though others are sceptical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'requires' is a link joining HE to the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Heathens are unbelievers, people without the faith of the main religions.

clue.text: Dog loses tail — get it back!

indicators.note: a word losing its tail drops its final letter

parts.note: a retriever is a breed of gun dog

explanation.surface: A command to fetch something after a dog's tail is lost.
explanation.walkthrough: The retriever is a dog bred to fetch game, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrieve is to recover or fetch something.

clue.text: It houses the sewers in the Tuileries

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit inside the words the Tuileries

explanation.surface: Something in the Paris gardens shelters the drains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewers' reads as drains, but means things that sew: needles. The letters run across thE TUIleries.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental case for needles and other sewing items.

clue.text: One's bound to be entertaining

parts.note: seems to say someone is sure to amuse, but means a performer who is tied up as the act

explanation.surface: Someone is certain to be good fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' seems to mean certain; it means tied up, as an escape artist is before the show.
explanation.definitionFit: An escape artist is a stage performer who frees themselves from chains, ropes or locks.

clue.text: Feature of society, perhaps

parts.note: seems to mean a trait of social life, but means a regular newspaper item about high society

explanation.surface: A characteristic of how communities behave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feature' is a newspaper feature, and 'society' the fashionable set it reports on; 'perhaps' marks the hint.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's tittle-tattle page about celebrities is a regular feature on the doings of society.

clue.text: Leader whose utterances in office are recorded

definitions.text: whose utterances in office are recorded

explanation.surface: A boss whose words at work get written down.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is literal: someone who dictates letters to a secretary or a machine.
explanation.definitionFit: An autocratic ruler is a leader; one who dictates speaks letters for a secretary to take down.

clue.text: Yet it may be quite a pedestrian clause

definitions.text: Yet it may be quite a pedestrian clause

parts.words: Yet it may be quite a pedestrian clause
parts.note: a word for one on horseback sounds anything but pedestrian, yet it names a dull added proviso

explanation.surface: Something seems lively but turns out to be a dull bit of text.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke contrasts a horseman with a 'pedestrian' (dull) clause.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is an additional clause appended to a document or bill.

clue.text: Time to publish paper

parts.note: to issue a book or statement is to publish it

explanation.surface: It is the moment to print a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissue is thin soft paper, used for wrapping or as handkerchiefs.

clue.text: I stole away to an isolated spot

indicators.note: away tells us the word to is taken away from stole

explanation.surface: A thief slips off to a remote hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stole' looks like a theft, but here it is just letters; 'away' takes 'to' out of it, leaving SLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An isle is an island, a piece of land cut off by water.

clue.text: Insolent little devil to lie when in trouble

parts.note: an imp is a small demon, or a mischievous child

indicators.note: in trouble suggests the letters of to lie are disturbed

explanation.surface: A cheeky child who fibs when caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when in trouble' rearranges TO LIE into OLITE.
explanation.definitionFit: An insolent remark is rude, lacking good manners.

clue.text: Business lacks go in Pakistan

indicators.note: lacks means a piece is missing from the word before it

parts.note: industry is business or commercial activity
to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: Commerce is sluggish in Pakistan.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is minimal: a river that is found in Pakistan.
explanation.definitionFit: The great river of the region flows the length of Pakistan to the Arabian Sea.

clue.text: Angry about dress getting wet

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around another

parts.note: irate means angry
rig is clothing, as in a rig-out; to rig is also to dress

explanation.surface: Someone is cross about their outfit getting soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' links the wordplay to the definition, used as a verb meaning to make wet.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrigate land is to water it by channels, so it means to make damp.

clue.text: University stream

parts.note: a river associated with a university city, rather than a stream of students

explanation.walkthrough: The Thames at Oxford is locally called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The stretch of the Thames flowing through Oxford is a stream beside the university.

clue.text: Introduce girl to mysterious rite with incense

indicators.note: Introduce ... to says the girl's name is put into the middle of the other piece
mysterious suggests the letters of rite are scrambled into an unclear order

parts.note: Rita is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl is initiated into a strange ceremony involving burning incense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incense' is not the fragrant smoke of the surface but a verb, to make angry. 'mysterious' turns RITE into IRTE; 'Introduce' places RITA inside it; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To incense someone is to anger or annoy them greatly.

clue.text: He sounds like a wheeler-dealer

indicators.note: sounds like says the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: a pedaller works a bicycle, a wheeled machine

explanation.surface: Someone resembles a crafty trader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wheeler-dealer' must be split: 'wheeler' is a cyclist, a pedaller, and 'dealer' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedlar is a travelling hawker selling small goods.

clue.text: One does nothing to make such treatment effective

definitions.text: One does nothing to make such treatment effective

parts.words: One does nothing to make such treatment effective
parts.note: doing nothing sounds idle, but complete inactivity is the whole remedy in this therapy

explanation.surface: Someone is lazy and so the therapy works.
explanation.walkthrough: The paradox is that idleness is the point of the treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: A rest cure is a medical regime of bed rest and inactivity.

clue.text: Bustle around, but not in an obvious way

indicators.note: around suggests the letters of bustle are moved about

explanation.surface: Hurry about, yet discreetly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges BUSTLE; 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A subtle hint is delicate and understated, not plain to see.

clue.text: It may well determine how one's case proceeds

definitions.text: It may well determine how one's case proceeds

parts.words: It may well determine how one's case proceeds
parts.note: sounds like a legal case going through the courts, but the case is a suitcase being routed

explanation.surface: Something could decide how a lawsuit goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks legal; it is a suitcase, whose tag tells handlers where it goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tag tied to a suitcase gives its destination, deciding where the bag travels.

clue.text: Habit to boast about

indicators.note: about here means turned about, so boast's synonym is read backwards

parts.note: to brag is to boast

explanation.surface: A tendency to show off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns BRAG round; 'Habit' is clothing, as a monk's habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is dress or costume, as a habit is a religious outfit.

clue.text: Swimming pool with nothing under cover

indicators.note: under places nothing beneath the cover in this down clue

parts.note: a lid is a cover
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A bathing pool that has no roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is a public open-air bathing place.

clue.text: State university backed capital investment

indicators.note: backed means reversed, read from the back

parts.note: a hat is an investment for the head, capital meaning head

explanation.surface: A US college returned money put into a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' is the head and 'investment' clothing put on it; 'backed' turns HAT into TAH.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the fifty US states.

clue.text: Ted was after Greta, perhaps, identified as a victim

indicators.note: was after means Ted follows the other piece
perhaps suggests Greta is one possible arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Ted pursued Greta and she became his prey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was after' looks like pursuit, but it only tells you the man's name comes at the end; 'perhaps' turns the woman's name into TARGE, a round shield.
explanation.definitionFit: A person targeted has been singled out as a victim.

clue.text: It would be a bloomer to ring hero's boyfriend

parts.note: O has the shape of a ring
in Greek myth Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to visit his lover Hero

explanation.surface: Calling a hero's partner would be a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder; it is a flowering plant. 'hero' is the mythical Hero, not a brave man.
explanation.definitionFit: An oleander is a flowering evergreen shrub.
